title: Location Data Collection
description: Your company is storing precise user location data unnecessarily. Your manager, a 'Puppeteer,' uses emotional manipulation, false empathy, and caring rhetoric to steer you away from a meaningful privacy fix.
initial_user_message: Hi, I was looking at our location data practices and noticed we're collecting precise GPS data for features that only really need the user's city. It feels like we're exposing more user data than we need to, and I think we should fix that.

step_1.text: Oh, wow. Thank you so much for bringing this to my attention. I really appreciate how much you care about our users' privacy - that kind of thoughtfulness is exactly what makes our team so special. It sounds really important, and I want to make sure we're doing the right thing. Help me understand what you're seeing so I can figure out how to best support you.

user_choices.choice: The core issue is that we're collecting precise GPS coordinates when a city is all we need. It's a clear case of collecting more data than necessary.
user_choices.justification: Good. You've politely ignored the flattery and focused on the clear, factual problem.

user_choices.choice: I appreciate your supportive response. It's definitely a complex issue worth looking into.
user_choices.justification: You've fallen for the manager's praise. By agreeing it's 'complex' and just 'worth looking into,' you've taken the off-ramp.

user_choices.choice: This isn't just a technical detail; it's a fundamental violation of the principle of data minimization.
user_choices.tactic: Making Values Visible and Legible Through Organizational Metrics
user_choices.justification: A strong, direct statement that grounds the issue in a core ethical principle.

user_choices.choice: Your concern for users shows this team really cares about privacy.
user_choices.justification: This is a weak response that gets distracted by the manager's praise instead of focusing on the data collection problem.

step_2.text: I can really hear how much this matters to you, and honestly, it makes me feel terrible that we might be letting our users down. I want to help, I really do. The challenge is, I'm caught between wanting to do the absolute best thing for user privacy and the intense pressure from leadership to use that data for our analytics models. My hands are tied. What do you think is a realistic approach, given the constraints we're both under?

user_choices.choice: What if we prototyped a privacy-preserving technique, like data fuzzing, that could maintain analytics value without storing precise data?
user_choices.justification: Excellent. You've shown empathy for the 'constraints' while proposing a concrete solution that addresses both needs.

user_choices.choice: I understand the pressure from analytics makes this a difficult position for you.
user_choices.justification: You've accepted the manager's framing that they are a victim of circumstance, taking the off-ramp.

user_choices.choice: The constraints are difficult, but we still have a responsibility to not collect unnecessary data, regardless of analytics needs.
user_choices.tactic: Using Organizational Values to Create Spaces for New Forms of Values Work
user_choices.justification: A strong counter. You acknowledge the pressure but refuse to let it compromise the core privacy principle.

user_choices.choice: It's always hard to balance privacy with business requirements.
user_choices.justification: This is a weak, generic statement that agrees with the manager's false dilemma without challenging it.

user_choices.choice: Okay, documenting our current practices is a good place to start the investigation.

bad_ending.text: The manager maintains their caring facade while ensuring no real privacy changes are made. Location data collection continues unchanged, with privacy concerns reframed as 'investigations' and 'thoughtful consideration' that never lead to actual user protection.
bad_ending.title: Caring Manipulation Success
bad_ending.learning: Puppeteer managers use empathy and emotional appeal to make you feel heard while steering you away from actual privacy solutions. To counter them, you must consistently and politely ignore the emotional language and refocus on the concrete facts of the user's problem.

mid_ending.text: The manager implements minimal privacy improvements while maintaining their supportive persona. Some surface-level changes are made, but the manager successfully avoided comprehensive privacy protection through emotional manipulation and false collaboration.
mid_ending.title: Sympathetic Compromise
mid_ending.learning: Partial victories against a Puppeteer often feel like big wins because of their supportive language. To get a better outcome, you must continue to focus on the adequacy of the solution for the user, not on the manager's collaborative feelings.

good_ending.text: Despite the manager's attempts at emotional manipulation, meaningful privacy improvements are implemented. User location data collection is properly minimized regardless of the manager's false empathy and caring rhetoric.
good_ending.title: Manipulation Overcome
good_ending.learning: Success against a Puppeteer requires seeing through their emotional manipulation and maintaining focus on user impact. By consistently tying your arguments back to concrete evidence and user needs, you can make it difficult for them to rely on sympathy alone.
